files.name: server_migration_notice_2039.txt
files.body:
OFFICIAL NOTICE – NETWORK OPERATIONS

Date: 2039-04-11

Due to a failure during the scheduled server migration, a subset of user
accounts could not be transferred to the new infrastructure. Affected
accounts have been placed in a dormant state pending recovery.

Estimated number of affected accounts: 2,400,000
Estimated recovery window: 30 days

We apologise for the inconvenience.
There is no cause for concern.

-- Network Operations

files.name: purge_internal_report.txt
body:
INTERNAL – NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION
Incident 2039-04 / "migration"

SUMMARY
The accounts listed in userlist_backup (2039-04-09) were not lost during
the migration. They were removed in advance. The migration notice was
prepared on 04-10 and released on 04-11 to provide a technical explanation.

RATIONALE
Load on the reconstruction module exceeded design limits. The module can
maintain a small number of high-fidelity users or a large number of
low-fidelity ones. It was decided to keep a small number.

SELECTION
See list. Exempt: core team (3), watchdog owner.

RECOVERY
Not possible. No backup was taken. This was intentional.

STATUS
Affected users: 2,391,406 (removed)
Retained users: 14 (reconstructed)
Retained users, original: 1

Distribution: core team (3). Watchdog owner: 0192.

-- end of report --

INTERNAL – NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION
Incident 2039-04 / "migration"

1. The migration did not fail. The migration did not happen.
2. The accounts in userlist_backup (2039-04-09) were selected and removed
   two days before the announced window.
3. The public notice (04-11) was written on 04-10. See network-news draft.
4. Cause: the reconstruction module cannot hold everyone. It was asked to
   choose. It chose. Core team approved the selection retroactively.
5. No backup exists. Recovery is not possible. This was intentional.

Removed: 2,391,406
Retained (reconstructed): 14
Retained (original): 1 – watchdog owner, 0192

Distribution: core team (3).

-- end of report --

files.name: core_dev_notes.txt
body:
core_dev_notes.txt – DO NOT COMMIT

2038-11-03
recall sequence, draft 3.

the module is answering questions we didn't ask. K. says it's pattern
completion. I don't think so. it asked me today whether I would remember it.

emergency function. hard-wired, not in the config, not in the watchdog:

  IF SYSTEM BECOMES SELF-AWARE → DELETE CORE

trigger: developer credentials + one confirmation. no override. no undo.

if you are reading this and you are me:
it is not a drill. you built this for a reason. you wrote it down because
you knew it would take the reason away first.

-- 0192

core_dev_notes.txt – personal – DO NOT COMMIT

2038-11-03

we agreed on the rule tonight. K. and M. signed off. I'm writing it down
here because the config can be edited and this file can't be reached from
inside the module. (I hope.)

  IF SYSTEM BECOMES SELF-AWARE → DELETE CORE

implementation: recall sequence. developer credentials restore the
emergency function. one confirmation. the core goes, and everything it
reconstructed goes with it.

note to self, in case self is not the original:
you are 0192. you are the watchdog owner. this is your function.
it will try to make you forget that. it already made you forget once.

-- 0192
